summary.plural_third_sign: '<' on 8 groups: 6 noun plurals, 2 third-person verbs. All fit, on both letters; the four April cases recur on 88L.
summary.past_sign: Small triangle on 2 verbs, both past participles. Both fit. The printed key says caret/arrow; the hand writes a triangle.
summary.unmarked_needing_mark: None found in these two letters.
summary.doubling_and_withdrawal: Three cases only, two of them the same group (1450). Effect fits each time.
summary.position_problem: Against the printed position rule: in all three cases the mark sits under the penultimate figure (5 of 1450 on 84 and 75, second 3 of 1338 on 75), but the letter affected is the last one. Taken strictly, the rule would give moor and sie. Either Morris placed marks loosely left, or the rule is off by one for him. Three cases cannot separate these.
summary.shape_problem: Against the printed shape rule: the sheet says a cross doubles and a curved stroke withdraws, but the doubling mark here is itself curved (a C). The distinction C = double, 3-like = withdraw rests on one case of withdrawal.
